newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Brit-Borneo enters bigger oil league.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Brit-Borneo enters bigger oil league.

text.p: British-Borneo, the investor darling among UK oil exploration firms, on Wednesday announced a 167.3 million pound ($280.5 million) rights issue, which will boost its size by about 20 percent.
The company also agreed to buy interests in three U.S. offshore blocks in another move to boost its strong niche position in deepwater Gulf of Mexico -- the current oil exploration hot spot.
British-Borneo agreed to buy from DuPont Co unit Conoco its 50 percent interests in the three blocks, which contain the King Kong gas field.

Additionally, British-Borneo Petroleum Syndicate Plc, which has seen its shares jump 72 percent so far this year, set a three-for-one stock split and forecast an unchanged 1997 dividend of 8.25 pence per share.
Finance Director Bill Colvin said British-Borneo was "moving to a different level of activity", becoming a medium-sized company with a wide range of undeveloped discoveries.
British-Borneo is heavily geared towards the Gulf of Mexico where it competes with giants such as Royal Dutch/Shell Group. But recently it also bought interests in the North Sea.
Without being more specific, the company said it also sees opportunities in other areas.
Its two-for-nine rights issue, priced at 1.2 pound per share, is aimed at supporting British-Borneo's increased operational activity.
The issue should also enhance British-Borneo's credibility with potential partners, the company said.
Colvin said there was "clearly a risk" that the company, which is highly geared to the deep water Gulf of Mexico, could attract the attention of a predator interested in the same area.
But he said the company was confident that if chairman Sir Bob Reid received "the dreaded phone call" from a company wanting to bid for British-Borneo it could persuade shareholders to stick with it.
British-Borneo shares fell 37-1/2 pence to 1.375 pounds following the rights issue, but several analysts saw scope for them to pick up again soon.
They argue equity issue strengthens the company's financial health and continue to stress British-Borneo's exciting prospects in the Gulf of Mexico.

"The key thing shareholders are really interested in is the return they are going to make on that exploration portfolio. We think that is good," said Colin Smith at broker BZW. ($ = 0.596 British Pounds)
